title: Test the full exposure map rather than only its code compression
statement: Given an operator-norm expansion K_gamma(T)P=U(T)(I-gamma B/2)P+O(gamma²),scalar first-order no-jump transparency holds exactly when BP=bP. PBP=bP alone misses(I-P)BP. The positive3x3 matrix with diagonal1 and B13=B31=1/2 gives an explicit scalar-compression counterexample.

requires: A justified bounded first-order expansion on the actual code
Self-adjoint exposure B and full output projection
provides: Necessary and sufficient conditional first-order transparency criterion and positive finite counterexample
assumptions: Remainder/domain estimates are supplied premises,not implied for arbitrary unbounded photon number
No claim that a particular device realizes the counterexample
costs: Compute the complete BP including off-code component; do not discard leakage
contract.units: Dimensionless half-diamond error and fidelity; oscillator time converts using angular frequency omega, not cycles. SI examples explicitly assume 5 GHz. Component values are model designs; losses are declared-model probabilities, not measurements.
contract.obstruction: Equal integrated code exposure is insufficient to classify all no-jump noise as erasure-only.
